description: Composite four-panel TEM figure of Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C (wt%) low-density steel after 50% cold-rolling reduction; three panels are TEM images and one is a diffraction pattern. (a) Bright-field TEM micrograph with a 500 nm scale bar: a heavily dislocated, banded dark/bright structure in which pairs of green dashed lines and the green label "microband" mark microband boundaries cutting the matrix. (b) Higher-magnification bright-field image (100 nm scale bar) of an intermittent linear structure: fine parallel striations traversing the field, decorated with dislocation clusters and tangles. (c) Selected-area diffraction pattern with the central (000) spot and two superimposed hexagonal sets of reflections drawn with dashed lines — blue for the matrix, labelled (1-11)_M, and green for the twin, labelled (111)_T/M and (–111)_T (arrowed). (d) Dark-field micrograph (100 nm scale bar) formed from the nano-twin (–111)_T reflection, showing very fine bright parallel lamellae on a black background. Taken together the panels demonstrate that the intermittent linear features in (b) are nano-scale deformation twins coexisting with microbands in the 50% rolled structure. No numeric values are printed on the panels; scale bars and the caption/citing text supply microband width 166 nm and twin thickness ~5.1 nm.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a bright-field TEM micrograph carrying a 500 nm scale bar, with pairs of green dashed lines and the green text label 'microband' annotating band boundaries in a heavily dislocated matrix.
Panel (b) is a bright-field TEM micrograph with a 100 nm scale bar showing an intermittent linear structure of thin parallel striations decorated with dislocation clusters and tangles.

Panel (c) is an SAED pattern with the central (000) spot and two superimposed hexagonal reflection nets indicated by blue and green dashed lines, the reflections labelled (1-11)_M, (111)_T/M and (–111)_T.
Panel (d) is a dark-field TEM micrograph with a 100 nm scale bar showing very fine bright parallel lamellae (nano-twins) on a dark background.

The caption states the images are of the 50% cold rolling reduction condition, that (a) and (b) are bright-field images, (c) is the selected-area diffraction pattern of the intermittent linear structure in (b), and (d) is a dark-field image from the nano-twin (–111)π reflection in (c).
The caption states the foil normal is [0 1 1]m, which is not verifiable from the pixels alone.
The caption labels the twin reflection as (–111)π whereas panel (c) prints the green label as (–111)_T; the two notations differ (π in the caption vs T = twin in the panel).
The citing text states the microbands formed at 50% reduction, indicated by pairs of green dashed lines in Fig. 5(a), have an average width of 166 nm.
The citing text states the deformation twins identified from the SADP and dark-field images are very fine, with an average thickness of ~5.1 nm.
The citing text states the average slip band spacing is 231 nm for the 30% reduction sample and 64 nm for the 50% reduction sample.

The citing text states that when the stress reaches ~1.5 GPa the microband structure and its intersections are well established, with microband boundaries formed by geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs).

The citing text states that different diffraction contrast within a single twin indicates a high dislocation density in the twin, and that the nano-scale twins form a fine T-M lamella structure (Fig. 5(d)).
No numeric values (dimensions, angles, intensities) are printed inside panels (a)–(d) other than the scale bars; all cited sizes come from the caption/citing text.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph, 500 nm scale bar, showing a heavily dislocated matrix with banded dark/bright contrast; pairs of green dashed lines plus the green text label 'microband' mark microband boundaries.

Bright-field TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, at higher magnification showing an intermittent linear structure: thin, roughly parallel dark/bright striations running across the image, decorated by clusters of dislocation debris and tangles.

Selected-area diffraction pattern with labelled central (000) spot; two superimposed hexagonal reflection nets drawn with dashed lines, blue for the matrix ((1-11)_M) and green for the twin ((111)_T/M and (–111)_T, arrowed). Foil normal stated as [0 1 1]_m.
Dark-field TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, formed from the nano-twin (–111)_T reflection: very fine, closely spaced bright parallel lamellae on a dark background.
